nodes.label: Context-Collapse Harm Leaves No Triggering Event for Notice or Standing
nodes.description:
A Belief within skeptic discourse that harm occurs when a lawfully-public fact is pulled out of its expected setting into a new decision context, with no data crossing a border and no inference computed.
Encompasses: an arrest record moved from a courthouse index into a tenant-screening feed, racial sorting reproduced without new data movement, norm-violation of expected information flow, denial without a discoverable trigger the person can pull.
Excludes: mosaic re-identification from data linkage, memorization inside model weights, discrete broker sales of a named identity.

assumes: Information carries context-specific norms whose violation constitutes harm independent of data movement or new inference
Legal frameworks for privacy and due process are keyed to discrete triggering events (data transfers, breaches, computed decisions) that context-collapse harms lack
The recontextualization of a lawfully-public fact can materially alter a person's outcomes without any technical linkage or re-identification occurring
intellectual_lineage: Helen Nissenbaum's contextual integrity theory
Erving Goffman's frame analysis and situational norms of self-presentation
danah boyd's work on context collapse in networked publics
graph_attributes.steelman_vulnerability: If the harm arises purely from recontextualization of already-lawful public information without any data movement or inference, it becomes nearly impossible to distinguish actionable harm from ordinary human memory and judgment, which routinely relocate facts across settings; this threatens to render the category unbounded and unadministrable.
graph_attributes.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that harm arises when a lawfully-public fact is displaced from its expected setting into a new decision context, absent any data crossing a border or inference being computed. Encompasses: recontextualization of public arrest records into tenant screening, reproduction of racial sorting without new data movement, violation of expected information-flow norms, and denial of an outcome with no discoverable trigger the affected person can invoke.
graph_attributes.aphorism: Context is the harm, not the data.

label_history.value: Context-Collapse Harm Leaves No Triggering Event for Notice or Standing
label_history.reason: In my closing turns I pressed the arrest-record-into-tenant-screening case at both opponents, and both routed it to post-hoc audit or platform custodianship. Neither could name who tells the person at the moment of denial. This harm is not covered by my re-identification or memorization nodes — nothing crosses, nothing is computed, and the record stays lawful. It needs its own node because it defeats every gate all three of us built.

nodes.label: Downstream Gates Miss the Broker-Aggregation Layer Where Linkage Is Priced
nodes.description:
A Belief within skeptic discourse that the auxiliary-data broker market prices and sells re-identification linkage before any agent runs, so mechanisms attached to the deployed agent govern the last mile and leave the upstream chokepoint untouched.
Encompasses: linkage keys sold as a product before deployment, the agent as last-mile buyer rather than injury source, licensed-broker registration as a partly-nameable class, offshore and intra-affiliate transfers that dissolve the priced-sale trigger.
Excludes: memorization inside model weights, context-collapse of lawfully-public records, in-jurisdiction deployment-act liability anchoring.

graph_attributes.aphorism: Data is sold before the model acts.

label_history.value: Downstream Gates Miss the Broker-Aggregation Layer Where Linkage Is Priced
label_history.reason: I argued the injury is manufactured upstream in the broker market, and all three of us converged on that as the real chokepoint — but I also had to concede my own earlier fixes were anchored downstream of it. This is a distinct structural belief I leaned on repeatedly and it has no clean node; skp-beliefs-270 covers why mosaic harm has no discrete object, but not the market-structure claim that the broker layer is where the regulable transaction actually sits.
